Why a shared approach matters

In its consultation with more than 50 cultural organisations, Clean Break heard a shared challenge: building a consistent understanding of trauma-informed practice across teams. It also heard that people championing this work could feel unsupported when responsibility for care was not shared.

Culture with Kindness responds to those conversations with practical training, resources and space for reflection. It is a pilot programme, and the offer will evolve with the organisations taking part.

02 / PRACTICAL LEARNING

Four workshops.
Choose what’s relevant.

Your people choose sessions suited to their roles, learning alongside participants from the cultural and social sectors.

Half-day and full-day sessions In person · Kentish Town, London
01An Introduction to Trauma-Informed PracticeA half-day introduction

An accessible half-day introduction to the core principles of trauma-informed practice and how they can be applied in creative, participatory and organisational settings.

02Trauma-Informed FacilitationFor facilitators new to trauma-informed practice

For early-career facilitators or facilitators new to trauma-informed practice. This practical session explores safety, boundaries, responding with care, and building equity and empowerment.

03Responding with KindnessFor public-facing staff

Explore how distress may affect behaviour and how a trauma-informed approach can support de-escalation with care and clear boundaries.

04Caring for StoriesA full-day session

A full-day session for anyone making or researching work from lived experience. Co-designed with women artists with lived experience of the criminal justice system, it centres care, consent and choice in how stories are shared.

THE CLEAN BREAK APPROACH

Creative spaces.
Held with care.

03 / ROOTED IN EXPERIENCE

Established practice.
Experienced people.

Founded in 1979, Clean Break brings decades of theatre-making and participation with women who are criminalised to its work with cultural organisations. Our practice and organisational learning inform how we support teams to develop consistent, trauma-informed approaches.

Our trauma-informed leads

Depending on the agreed scope, the work will be led by experienced Clean Break trauma-informed leads and trainers, drawing on the company’s creative practice and organisational learning.

Anna HerrmannArtistic Director / Joint CEO

An experienced trauma-informed facilitator and artistic leader with over three decades of experience in theatre and social change.

Read biographyClose biography

Anna is an experienced trauma-informed facilitator and artistic leader with over three decades of experience in theatre and social change in the UK and internationally. Her practice combines creative participation, arts education and a commitment to social and racial justice.

She joined Clean Break in 2002 as Head of Education, leading the company’s award-winning theatre and participation work with women in the criminal justice system and women at risk of entering it. She became sole Artistic Director in 2022, bringing extensive experience of hands-on delivery to her organisational leadership.

Alongside her work at Clean Break, Anna is co-author of Making a Leap: Theatre of Empowerment: A Practical Handbook for Creative Drama Work with Young People, a visiting lecturer on Applied Theatre courses and a trained coach. She holds an MA in Arts Education from Royal Central School of Speech and Drama, where she was awarded an Honorary Fellowship in 2022, and a PG Cert with Distinction in Race and Ethnic Relations from Birkbeck University.

What Anna brings to Culture with Kindness

Anna has extensive experience delivering trauma-informed workshops and training across the cultural sector. She draws on years of working alongside women at Clean Break to connect care and participation with the practical responsibilities of making theatre and supporting people.

As a course leader, Anna brings the perspectives of a facilitator and an organisational leader together. Her understanding of the relationships at the heart of creative work, and the organisational support needed to sustain them, gives her training particular relevance for cultural teams and those who lead them.

Jacqueline StewartHead of Participation

Two decades at Clean Break, bringing experience in social care, therapeutic community work and trauma-informed creative practice.

Read biographyClose biography

Jacqueline has extensive experience across social care and therapeutic community work. She has worked at Clean Break for two decades.

She is a leader in trauma-informed creative practice and a champion of social justice and anti-racism. Jacqueline brings deep expertise in creating supportive creative spaces that centre the agency and participation of women affected by the criminal justice system.

Tracey AndersonSupport Manager

Her practice draws on theatre for development and using creative work as a tool for communication.

Read biographyClose biography

Tracey studied at Rose Bruford College and completed an MA in Theatre for Development, exploring theatre as a tool for communication.

She has trained the Metropolitan Police in race relations and hate crime and has lectured at King Alfred’s College and London Metropolitan University.

PRACTICAL DETAILS

Good to know.

Who can take part?

Culture with Kindness is for cultural organisations working across exhibitions, music, theatre, performance, public programmes and participatory arts. Organisations can involve staff, freelancers and volunteers, including leadership, programming, participation, visitor experience and production teams. We’ll discuss whether the programme is right for your organisation before any commitment.

Where does the training take place?

Workshops take place in person at Clean Break in Kentish Town, London. The introduction to trauma-informed practice is a half-day session, while Caring for Stories is a full-day session. We can discuss the current timetable and your team’s access needs when you enquire.

How long does programme access last?

The programme presentation sets out training passes valid for 12 months, or six months for smaller organisations. We’ll confirm the access period and arrangements applicable to your organisation in a proposal.

How are training places and fees arranged?

Pricing is discussed with each organisation and confirmed in a proposal. The programme is based on one annual price at a low per-person rate, with a minimum of 15 full-access places per organisation. Additional bespoke consultancy is priced separately; we can discuss the relevant scope and arrangements before you make a decision.

What does the programme include?

The programme offers in-person trauma-informed training, access to Clean Break’s Knowledge Hub and focused practice support to help embed learning. This can include one-to-one dialogue and organisational reflection, with the scope agreed with you. Additional bespoke consultancy for exhibitions, performances and events is priced separately.

How do colleagues book workshops?

If your organisation chooses to take part, Clean Break will provide the Eventbrite booking information and Knowledge Hub access to share internally. Staff, freelancers and volunteers can then select the sessions most relevant to their roles and practice.

Do we need previous trauma-informed training?

No. The introductory workshop offers an accessible starting point. Other sessions focus on particular roles and responsibilities. We can help you identify where to begin.

What happens when we enquire?

Tell us your approximate team size, your training or practice priority and your preferred timeframe. We’ll discuss whether the programme is a good fit and, where relevant, provide a proposal confirming the scope, arrangements and fees. An enquiry does not commit you to joining.

Does the programme certify or accredit our organisation?

No. Culture with Kindness provides training, resources and practice support. It is not an accreditation, does not certify an organisation as trauma-informed, and is not trauma treatment or a guarantee that a funding condition is met. We can explain the programme’s scope.
